prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules recruit ubiquitin ligases to destroy chosen proteins, through the PROTAC concept and the identification of cereblon as the target through which glue degraders act

statement.case_for: I keep targeted protein degradation (B020) as the whole prize, with the same three names as in round 1. After reading all eight statements, the support is not only a matter of count: every member who engages with the chemistry names the same principle, a small molecule that induces a ligase-target ternary complex so that removal of the protein is catalytic and event-driven rather than occupancy-based. That principle is physical-chemical in a way I can judge from my own field. It depends on interfacial protein-protein recognition, cooperativity and linker geometry, and it is supported by structures and kinetics, by independent reproduction, and by a very large body of follow-up work. The two halves of the citation are complementary: Crews and Deshaies conceived recruiting a ligase to a chosen protein, and Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, which explains how a drug already in patients works through the same ligase-proximity mechanism. One citation can therefore honestly cover both without implying two prizes. Round 1 did not give me a reason to prefer a different configuration, and the chair's questions make me more, not less, sure that a single-part prize is cleaner than adding a second part.
statement.case_against: No PROTAC is approved yet, so the claim of transformed medicine still rests on concept, mechanism and early clinical data. A three-person limit leaves out Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito, and Sakamoto and Kim as authors of the 2001 PROTAC paper are the omissions I find hardest to defend. The bifunctional and glue lineages have different inventors and histories, so a combined citation can be read as a compromise. Finally, Peter Brzezinski's concern that this is medicinal chemistry and pharmacology that Medicine could equally claim is real; I answer it by emphasising the chemical mechanism in the citation, but it is a judgment and not a settled point.

responses.point: Johan keeps B020 as the prize but names Ciulli as third laureate and limits the citation to bifunctional degraders, and he says B061 is the better prize if the committee finds the clinical evidence too immature.
responses.response: I take his scientific point that Ciulli's structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex work turned the PROTAC concept into rational design, and I do not think a citation that omits Ciulli is comfortable. But I stay with Handa for the third seat, for a reason that is about the chemistry and not the head count: a bifunctional-only citation leaves the cereblon mechanism outside the prize, and that mechanism is what explains the one degrader-type drug class already used in patients. Ciulli refined a modality whose concept was already set; Handa supplies the molecular identification that the glue field could not do without. On his fallback, I accept that B061 is the cleanest attribution on the shortlist and is mature, but I do not think the maturity of a method within theory should override a concept that has changed how small-molecule pharmacology is conceived. I would keep B061 as an alternative and a serious candidate for a later year.

responses.point: Andrei proposes a two-part prize: Liu alone for base editing (B047) plus Crews and Deshaies for degraders (B020), arguing that Liu-only is defensible and that base editing is a distinct chemical transformation.
responses.response: His argument that adenine base editing needed directed evolution of a DNA-acting deaminase, and so is more than a repackaging of CRISPR, moved me on the chemistry; I now regard B047 as a stronger alternative than I did in round 1, and I agree that Liu alone is the only attribution I could defend, since I was uneasy about naming two trainees while the Kondo and Nishida Target-AID priority question is open. I still do not support the pairing. It would cut the B020 attribution to two names and drop Handa, which separates the PROTAC concept from the cereblon mechanism that explains why glue degraders work; and joining two young therapeutic-adjacent fields in one year, one of them close to the 2020 prize and the other without an approved drug, seems to me to compound the maturity risk instead of balancing it. If the committee decides B020 is not ready, B047 with Liu alone is where I would look next.

responses.point: Peter supports Crews, Deshaies and Handa but raises the worry that targeted degradation is a medicinal chemistry and pharmacology achievement that the Medicine committee could just as readily claim, and asks whether PROTAC and glue strands should be one citation or two parts.
responses.response: I think the Medicine worry is best answered by what the citation says. The achievement is a mechanism and a chemical design principle: induced proximity through a ternary complex, with its cooperativity, linker and interfacial recognition, and the identification of cereblon as a ligase substrate receptor that a small molecule can redirect. None of that is a therapeutic outcome, and it is why I would word the citation around the chemistry and not around a drug class. I would keep it as one part rather than two because both strands rest on the same ternary-complex mechanism; splitting would give two parts with up to four or five names across them, which exceeds the three-person ceiling for the whole configuration, and would give the impression of two unfinished prizes. I accept that this leaves the medicinal chemistry boundary a judgment call that he and I may weigh differently.

responses.point: Heiner, the chair, shares the Crews, Deshaies and Handa configuration and says the open question is whether Ciulli should replace Handa and whether the glue and PROTAC strands are one achievement or two.
responses.response: We agree on the configuration, and the chair's round-1 question about the third seat has not changed my answer: Handa, because the cereblon identification is the mechanistic pillar that lets one citation span both strands. I also agree with his Liu-only reading of base editing, and I share his concern about closeness to the 2020 prize; that is part of why I put B047 as an alternative and not as a second part. On maturity, I would accept an award without an approved PROTAC if the committee records that structures, independent reproduction and the mechanistic explanation of cereblon, and not a clinical approval, are the basis, which is the standard the Chemistry prize has applied before. What would change my view is clinical data that contradicted the event-driven mechanism, and nothing in round 1 suggests that.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept Handa rather than Ciulli as third laureate, and whether a single citation can fairly span PROTACs and cereblon-based glue degraders without implying that Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito were not contributors.
Whether the absence of an approved PROTAC drug should delay the prize; I treat it as tolerable, but I could be wrong about how much weight colleagues give to early clinical outcomes.
Whether B047 with Liu alone is distinct enough from the 2020 CRISPR prize and whether the Kondo and Nishida priority question can be settled.
I am working from the shortlist and colleagues' statements and have not checked dates for the 2001 PROTAC paper or the 2010 cereblon work independently.
statement.conflict_note: Unchanged from round 1 in substance. My lipid self-assembly and lipid-protein co-assembly work is close to ionizable lipid nanoparticles (B010) and biomolecular condensates (B024); neither is in my preferred configuration, and I would not lead a decision on them. My alternatives B047 and B061 are outside my own research area. I sit on the committee with Lund colleagues Heiner Linke and Peter Somfai, which I do not regard as a recusal issue. I have no personal connection to Crews, Deshaies or Handa.
